scenes.text: You’ve probably noticed that our modern roads crack and crumble after just a few years, yet ancient Roman concrete structures are still standing strong after two thousand years.
For centuries, scientists couldn’t figure out how Roman harbors survived crashing waves, violent earthquakes, and time itself, but the mind-blowing secret was actually hidden in plain sight.
They recently discovered that tiny white mineral chunks inside the concrete, once dismissed as poor mixing, act as a catalyst that triggers self-healing whenever rainwater seeps into a crack.
Imagine if our modern cities could automatically repair themselves just like living skin, so tell us in the comments if you would trust a self-healing concrete house.
